comment: Seccomp profile for bcp_pipeline container. Allows all Docker-default syscalls and additionally blocks dangerous syscalls related to mount privilege escalation, kernel module loading, and memory introspection.

syscalls.comment: Block mount-related syscalls: CVE-2026-27456, CVE-2026-53612, CVE-2026-53613, CVE-2026-53614, CVE-2026-53615 (util-linux TOCTOU / privilege escalation via mount)
Block kernel module loading (container should never load kernel modules)
Block cross-process memory access: CVE-2019-1010025 (pthread heap address disclosure), CVE-2019-1010023 (ldd code exec via malicious ELF)
Block BPF and perf events (can be abused for privilege escalation and info leakage: CVE-2019-1010022, CVE-2019-1010024)
Block swap and hostname changes (not needed by bcp_pipeline)

Block obsolete/legacy syscalls not needed by bcp_pipeline (oprofile dcookie lookup, legacy NFS server control, x86 vm86 mode). General attack-surface reduction; NOT specific to CVE-2026-53615 (see dedicated ioctl rules below for that).

CVE-2026-53615 (libblkid DoS via partition-table integer overflow): block BLKGETSIZE64 (0x80081272=2148012658) and legacy BLKGETSIZE (0x1260=4704) ioctl requests, the primary calls used to probe block-device/partition geometry before parsing partition data. Supplementary defense only -- the primary mitigation is that docker-compose_vm1_secure.yml grants no `devices:`/`--device`/privileged access, so the container has no block-device nodes (/dev/sd*, /dev/nvme*, /dev/loop*) to issue these ioctls against in the first place. Other ioctl requests (FIONREAD, TCGETS, ODBC/socket ioctls) remain allowed via defaultAction.

CVE-2025-69720 (ncurses buffer overflow): block TIOCSTI (0x5412=21522) and TIOCLINUX (0x541C=21532) ioctl requests, which are the classic tty-injection / terminal-escape primitives used to drive ncurses rendering paths. bcp_pipeline never allocates a tty, so these requests are never legitimate. Other ioctl requests (FIONREAD, TCGETS, ODBC/socket ioctls) remain allowed via defaultAction.
CVE-2025-69720: block TIOCLINUX ioctl (terminal screen-dump/selection injection)
